body:
I think both cases are valid, in some cases anyone think keeping section is ideal, and in other cases resetting is desirable.

So my opinion is that we should clear section by default and add an additional argument to stop() like `stop(bool keep_state = false, bool keep_section = false)`. How do you think @chocola-mint ?

@TokageItLab So I looked into this a bit further.

I believe the confusion stems from this part in [`AnimationPlayer.play`'s documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_animationplayer.html#class-animationplayer-method-play):
> The **AnimationPlayer** keeps track of its current or last played animation with `assigned_animation`. If this method is called with that same animation `name`, or with no `name` parameter, the assigned animation will resume playing if it was paused.

Technically, the current behavior is doing just that.
- The section is cleared correctly. (I've double-checked with the debugger)
- The playback position, however, is not necessarily reset to 0. Instead, it resumes from the "start" that `stop()` saw when it was called. Which is to say:
  - When `play_section_with_markers()` gets stopped with `stop()`, the playback position is set back to the start of the section automatically. (with `seek()`)
  - When `play()` gets called, the playback resumes from the current playback position, which is the start of the previous section. The section being played is updated correctly here.

In my opinion, I think the problem is that `stop()`'s reset position may not always be what the user wants. Currently they may need to call `seek()` one more time explicitly after `stop()` to adjust the reset position to what they want. This is not a bug but a limitation of the current API. (Although calling `seek()` twice is pretty wasteful and could be avoided with better API)

We could introduce an additional `reset_time` parameter to `stop()` to address this limitation. Does this sound good to you?
@chocola-mint Isn't `reset_time` synonymous with `keep_state`? See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71218 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71619.

@chocola-mint I cannot understand what you meaning. I am suggesting the following four patterns:

stop(bool p_keep_state = false, bool p_keep_section = false):
- stop(false, false)
  - Clear section and reset position to 0
- stop(true, false)
  - Clear section and don't move the position
- stop(false, true)
  - Keep section and reset position to section's start point
- stop(true, true)
  - Keep section and don't move the position

Then I think the AnimationPlayerEditor changes the argument depending on whether or not a section is enabled (if the internal value of section is negative, we can determine section is invalid).

So is `reset_time` intended for any other use case? I feel it would be odd to “reset” the animation into the position other than the above. I think that basically it is enough to get the starting point of the section and reset it there, and the only implementation needed here is whether or not to clear the section before that starting point retrieval.

FYI, I remember there was a reason why `seek()` is used on reset, to reset the animation state (with TRS3D/BlendShape/Value/Bezier/AnimationPlayback tracks) at the reset position.

@TokageItLab 

The playback position is always reset to the start of the current section, regardless of `keep_state`. It's just that setting `keep_state` to false will cause `stop()` to use `seek()`, evaluating the animation immediately so it looks that way.

See below: (Line 778 and 781 in particular) 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/animation/animation_player.cpp#L770-L787

**There's no "section" that needs clearing.** In `AnimationPlayer.play`, it does play the new section assigned to it correctly. It's just that, to match the behavior described in the documentation, (if playing the same animation, resume from the previous playback position) **it will start the playback from `playback.current.pos`**, which happens to be set to the start of the previous section played. (Again, regardless if `keep_state` was true or not, as seen above)

To put it in another way, the current behavior of `stop(bool p_keep_state = false)` is as follows:
- `stop(false)`
  - Reset playback position to section's start point internally, but do not evaluate the start point.
- `stop(true)`
  - Reset playback position to section's start point with `seek()`, evaluating the start point immediately and updating the animation's visuals, etc.

I propose `stop(bool p_keep_state = false, float p_reset_time = -1.0f)`:
- `stop(false, negative_value)` (equivalent to the current `stop(false)`)
  - Reset playback position to section's start point internally, but do not evaluate the start point.
- `stop(true, negative_value)` (equivalent to the current `stop(true)`)
  - Reset playback position to section's start point with `seek()`, evaluating the start point immediately and updating the animation's visuals, etc.
- `stop(false, non_negative_value)`
  - Reset playback position to `non_negative_value` internally, but do not evaluate the animation at that point.
- `stop(true, non_negative_value)`
  - Reset playback position to `non_negative_value` with `seek()`, evaluating the start point immediately and updating the animation's visuals, etc.

`non_negative_value` can be set to 0 if the user knows that they want to play the same animation from the start but with no sections. And, it can be set to a different marker's time if they know they want to play the same animation from the start but with a different section.

> Reset playback position to non_negative_value with seek(), evaluating the start point immediately and updating the animation's visuals, etc.

I say this is difinitly odd. The reset must jump to the "beginning of the section" or "beginning of the animation". It is obviously overstepping the role of "stop" to jump to any point that has no static meaning as a beginning point.

Honestly I'm fine with whatever, but I'm just making it clear that "the position `playback.current.pos` is set to after `stop()`" is the problem here and if there's going to be a solution, it's going to be changing that in particular. Whether it's adding an option to always set it to 0, some other number that the user can specify, or just telling the user to call `seek()` again after `stop()` themselves.
